alt: A table of major CNN architectures with year and main contribution: LeNet-5 (1998), AlexNet (2012), VGGNet (2014), GoogLeNet Inception (2014), ResNet (2015), DenseNet (2017) and EfficientNet (2019).
author: Deep Learning faculty

alt: A Quick Memory box: LeNet is the birth of CNN, AlexNet made CNN powerful with deep learning, GPU and ReLU, VGG is deeper with small filters, GoogLeNet uses parallel Inception modules, ResNet uses skip connections, EfficientNet gives better efficiency. A time arrow runs from early to modern.
author: Deep Learning faculty

alt: A comparison table of LeNet-5 and AlexNet by year, application, input, depth, activation, pooling, GPU, dropout, data augmentation and importance.
author: Deep Learning faculty

alt: Very brief pictures of other major CNNs: VGGNet stacks many small 3 by 3 filters, GoogLeNet has parallel convolutions with different filter sizes, ResNet has a skip connection around convolutions, DenseNet connects each layer to many later layers and EfficientNet scales depth, width and resolution.
author: Deep Learning faculty

alt: A panel titled What is LeNet-5 with the simple definition: LeNet-5 is a CNN architecture designed for handwritten digit recognition, which uses convolution, subsampling or pooling, and fully connected layers to automatically learn features from images and classify them.
author: Deep Learning faculty

alt: The LeNet-5 architecture drawn left to right: input 32 by 32 by 1, C1 convolution 28 by 28 by 6, S2 subsampling 14 by 14 by 6, C3 convolution 10 by 10 by 16, S4 subsampling 5 by 5 by 16, C5 convolution 1 by 1 by 120, F6 fully connected 84, output 10 classes.
author: Deep Learning faculty

alt: A panel titled Important Ideas in LeNet-5: convolution detects edges, curves and shapes, subsampling or pooling halves a 28 by 28 map to 14 by 14 and reduces computation, and hierarchical feature learning goes from edges to curves to parts of digits to the complete digit.
author: Deep Learning faculty

alt: A panel titled LeNet vs Traditional Fully Connected Network. A fully connected network connects every pixel to many neurons, giving a huge number of parameters and ignoring spatial structure. LeNet has far fewer parameters, preserves spatial information and learns features automatically.
author: Deep Learning faculty

alt: Two panels. Why is it called LeNet-5: it has five trainable layers C1, C3, C5, F6 and Output, and pooling layers S2 and S4 are not counted. Important characteristics: 32 by 32 by 1 grayscale input, 6 filters of 5 by 5, 16 filters, 120 filters, 2 by 2 subsampling, 84 neurons, 10 classes, tanh.
author: Deep Learning faculty

alt: LeNet-5 in one simple example. A handwritten 8 goes through C1 which finds edges, S2 which reduces size, C3 which finds curves and shapes, S4 which reduces size, C5 which combines complex features, F6 which makes the final representation and the output where the 8 has the highest score.
author: Deep Learning faculty

alt: A layer by layer table of LeNet-5 with operation, input size, number of filters or neurons, filter size, output size and what each layer learns. Input 32 by 32 by 1, C1 28 by 28 by 6, S2 14 by 14 by 6, C3 10 by 10 by 16, S4 5 by 5 by 16, C5 1 by 1 by 120, F6 84, Output 10.
author: Deep Learning faculty

alt: What is happening conceptually in LeNet-5. The shapes 32 by 32 by 1, 28 by 28 by 6, 14 by 14 by 6, 10 by 10 by 16, 5 by 5 by 16, 1 by 1 by 120, 84, 10 with the job of each layer, and an example softmax output where digit 5 has the highest score 0.82.
author: Deep Learning faculty

alt: A panel titled AlexNet. AlexNet is a deep CNN architecture developed by Alex Krizhevsky, Ilya Sutskever and Geoffrey Hinton in 2012, famous for a major breakthrough in large-scale image classification on the ImageNet competition. It showed that a deep CNN trained with GPUs and large data can learn features and perform much better.
author: Deep Learning faculty

alt: A table of the key features of AlexNet: deep CNN, ReLU instead of sigmoid or tanh in hidden layers, max pooling, GPU training, dropout to reduce overfitting, a large dataset (ImageNet) and automatic feature learning.
author: Deep Learning faculty

alt: The basic AlexNet architecture as a vertical list: input image 227 by 227 by 3, convolution 1 with ReLU and max pooling, convolution 2 with ReLU and max pooling, convolutions 3, 4 and 5 with ReLU and a max pooling, then fully connected FC6, FC7 and the output.
author: Deep Learning faculty

alt: How AlexNet learns features: image, edges, shapes, textures, object parts, objects, getting more abstract. Early layers learn simple patterns and deeper layers learn complex patterns and objects.
author: Deep Learning faculty

alt: The AlexNet architecture left to right with sizes: input 227 by 227 by 3, Conv1 55 by 55 by 96, max pool 27 by 27 by 96, Conv2 27 by 27 by 256, max pool 13 by 13 by 256, Conv3 and Conv4 13 by 13 by 384, Conv5 13 by 13 by 256, max pool 6 by 6 by 256, flatten 9216, FC6 4096, FC7 4096 and output 1000 with softmax.
author: Deep Learning faculty

alt: Two panels. Why was ResNet needed: people made CNNs deeper from 10 to 100 layers expecting better accuracy, but training became difficult and accuracy stopped improving or even decreased, the degradation problem. Why deep networks become difficult: vanishing gradients, harder learning, degradation of training accuracy. ResNet solves it by skipping some layers with a shortcut connection.
author: Deep Learning faculty

alt: Two panels. What is a residual: let the desired output be H of x, ResNet learns F of x equal to H of x minus x, so H of x equals F of x plus x. An easy example: original information x plus newly learned information F of x gives the final representation x plus F of x.
author: Deep Learning faculty

alt: A panel titled Residual Block, the basic building block. The input x goes through a convolution with W1, ReLU and a convolution with W2, and also travels along a shortcut. The two are added to give F of x plus x, then activation. Output y equals F of x plus x.
author: Deep Learning faculty

alt: A panel titled When input and output sizes are different. If the convolution layers change height, width or channels the shortcut cannot be added directly, so a projection shortcut with a 1 by 1 convolution makes the dimensions compatible.
author: Deep Learning faculty

alt: A panel titled Why are skip connections important. Without a skip connection the signal passes through layers 1 to 100 one after another. With skip connections a shortcut gives information and gradients a more direct path through the network.
author: Deep Learning faculty

alt: A panel titled Advantages of ResNet: it allows very deep networks of tens to hundreds of layers, helps gradient flow through shortcut connections, reduces the degradation problem and gives better feature learning. It is used for image classification, object detection, image segmentation, face recognition, medical image analysis and transfer learning.
author: Deep Learning faculty

alt: The ResNet overall architecture for the example ResNet-18 with output sizes: input 224 by 224 by 3, 7 by 7 convolution with 64 filters giving 112 by 112 by 64, 3 by 3 max pool giving 56 by 56 by 64, four residual block groups of 64, 128, 256 and 512 channels, global average pooling 1 by 1 by 512, fully connected 1000 and softmax.
author: Deep Learning faculty

alt: The GoogLeNet architecture left to right: input 224 by 224 by 3, Conv1 7 by 7, max pool, Conv2 1 by 1, Conv3 3 by 3, max pool, Inception modules (3a and 3b, 4a to 4e, 5a and 5b) giving 28 by 28 by 256, 14 by 14 by 480 and 7 by 7 by 1024, average pool 7 by 7, dropout, fully connected 1000 and softmax.
author: Prof. Karishma Raut

alt: An example Inception module and its benefits. Four parallel branches (1 by 1 then 3 by 3, 1 by 1 then 5 by 5, 1 by 1 only, and 3 by 3 max pool then 1 by 1) are concatenated depth-wise. It captures multi-scale features, the 1 by 1 convolutions reduce dimensions, and outputs are joined along the channels.
author: Prof. Karishma Raut

alt: The naive Inception module. The previous layer feeds parallel 1 by 1, 3 by 3 and 5 by 5 convolutions and a 3 by 3 max pooling, and the results are joined by filter concatenation.
author: Prof. Karishma Raut

alt: The Inception module with dimension reduction. A 1 by 1 convolution is added before the 3 by 3 and 5 by 5 convolutions and after the 3 by 3 max pooling, to cut computation, and the four branches are joined by filter concatenation.
author: Prof. Karishma Raut

alt: The VGG-16 architecture: input 224 by 224 by 3, five blocks of 3 by 3 convolutions (2, 2, 3, 3 and 3 convolutions with 64, 128, 256, 512 and 512 filters) each ending with a 2 by 2 max pool that halves the size from 224 to 14, then fully connected 4096, 4096 and 1000 with softmax.
author: Prof. Karishma Raut

alt: The VGG-16 detailed configuration table: Block 1 224 by 224 with 64 filters, Block 2 112 by 112 with 128, Block 3 56 by 56 with 256, Block 4 28 by 28 with 512, Block 5 14 by 14 with 512, each followed by max pool, then FC6 4096, FC7 4096 and FC8 1000.
author: Prof. Karishma Raut

alt: The VGG ConvNet configurations A to E from 11 to 19 weight layers. All use 3 by 3 convolutions with 64, 128, 256, 512 and 512 filters separated by max pooling, then FC-4096, FC-4096, FC-1000 and softmax. Column D has 16 weight layers.
author: Prof. Karishma Raut

alt: The ResNet-50 architecture: input 224 by 224 by 3, 7 by 7 convolution with 64 filters, max pool, four stages of 3, 4, 6 and 3 residual blocks giving 56 by 56 by 256, 28 by 28 by 512, 14 by 14 by 1024 and 7 by 7 by 2048, global average pooling and fully connected 1000 with softmax.
author: Prof. Karishma Raut

alt: The ResNet-50 architecture summary table with output size, layers and number of blocks for each stage from input to the fully connected layer.
author: Prof. Karishma Raut

alt: The U-Net architecture drawn as a U. The left side is the contracting path where blocks of two 3 by 3 convolutions with ReLU are followed by 2 by 2 max pooling and the number of channels doubles from 64 to 1024. The right side is the expansive path with 2 by 2 up-convolutions, copy and crop skip connections from the left, and a final 1 by 1 convolution to the segmentation map.
author: Prof. Karishma Raut

alt: A merits and demerits table for LeNet and AlexNet. LeNet used spatial correlation to cut computation and learned feature hierarchies automatically, but scaled poorly, used large filters and learned only low-level features. AlexNet extracted low, mid and high-level features, introduced regularization and used GPUs, but had dormant neurons in the first layers and aliasing from large filters.
author: Prof. Karishma Raut

alt: The LeNet-5 architecture with a short note under each layer: input 32 by 32 grayscale, C1 6 filters of 5 by 5, S2 average pooling 2 by 2 stride 2, C3 16 filters, S4 average pooling, C5 120 filters acting like a fully connected layer, F6 84 neurons and the output layer of 10 neurons for digits 0 to 9.
author: Prof. Karishma Raut

alt: A comparison table of LeNet-5, AlexNet and VGGNet-16 by architecture diagram, key building block, depth, parameters, input, design philosophy, strengths and limitations.
author: Prof. Karishma Raut

alt: The same comparison table for GoogLeNet, ResNet-50 and U-Net: architecture diagram, key building block, depth, parameters, input, design philosophy, strengths, limitations and typical applications.
author: Prof. Karishma Raut

alt: The class drawing of Sum 1. A 32 by 32 by 3 input goes through 10 filters of 5 by 5 by 3 with stride 1 and padding 2 and gives 10 feature maps of 32 by 32, so the output is 32 by 32 by 10. One filter has 5 times 5 times 3 equals 75 weights plus 1 bias equals 76 parameters, and 10 filters give 760 parameters.
author: Deep Learning faculty

alt: The complete architecture of Sum 2. A 100 by 100 by 3 image goes through convolution layer 1 with 8 filters of 3 by 3 by 3 (stride 1, padding 0) to give 98 by 98 by 8, then convolution layer 2 with 1 filter of 3 by 3 by 8 to give 96 by 96 by 1. Total parameters 224 plus 73 equals 297.
author: Deep Learning faculty

alt: The summary table of Sum 2 with input, filters, filter size, stride, padding, output and parameters for the two layers (224 and 73 parameters), and the easy method of four steps: output size, output depth, parameters F times F times D plus 1 times K, and use the previous output as the next input.
author: Deep Learning faculty

alt: The diagram of a 224 by 224 by 3 RGB input passing through 5 kernels of 7 by 7 and giving an output of 218 by 218 by 5, which is 5 feature maps.
author: Deep Learning faculty
